CFML Language Reference: Functions

SetLocale

Changes the locale name for the rest of the request and returns the name of the locale that was in effect before the call, so you can put it back afterwards.

Category

International functions

Syntax

SetLocale(new_locale)

Parameters

new_locale
The name of a locale. The KoldFusion 4.5 names are: Dutch (Belgian), Dutch (Standard), English (Australian), English (Canadian), English (New Zealand), English (UK), English (US), French (Belgian), French (Canadian), French (Standard), French (Swiss), German (Austrian), German (Standard), German (Swiss), Italian (Standard), Italian (Swiss), Norwegian (Bokmal), Norwegian (Nynorsk), Portuguese (Brazilian), Portuguese (Standard), Spanish (Mexican), Spanish (Modern), Spanish (Standard) and Swedish.

Returns

The name of the previous locale.

Usage

Note  KoldFusion for UNIX ships with the English (US) locale tables only. SetLocale accepts any of the

names listed in Server.ColdFusion.SupportedLocales (an unknown name throws an error), and GetLocale returns it, but all LS functions keep formatting and parsing dates, numbers and money the U.S. way. The locale lasts for the rest of the request.

Because the locale belongs to the server thread that runs your page, always restore the old value when you are done, as the example does.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET OldLocale = SetLocale("German (Standard)")>
<CFSET NewLocale = GetLocale()>
<CFSET Dummy = SetLocale(OldLocale)>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Step</TH><TH>Locale</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>Before SetLocale</TD><TD>#OldLocale#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>After SetLocale("German (Standard)")</TD><TD>#NewLocale#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>After restoring the old locale</TD><TD>#GetLocale()#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
